title: The trombonist John Degrass and Norwegian ladies
summary: Butler marvels at trombonist John Degrass and drummer Walter Johnson picking up women at a Norwegian hotel while the Cubans quarrelled over them; they left in July 1939.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: John, he played the trombone. John could snatch more women. John culd snatch more women in the a street called Radhust Gaten hotel -- we was living in/ (inaudible) and John opened the door and the chick, he snatch her and close the door and then, about an hour later, because those people are very punctual, they come on time. Well, about an hour or hour and a half later, wham, John had snatched one.
I said, John, I don't know what -- there's something, you don't know what they do, but every time he is, whatever they do, they got a chick.
Walter Johnson was one of them kind. He would be playing his drums and chewing chewing gum and at the end, come on, baby, and he's gone. And I didn't know what them people was doing.

John, degrass he was playing the trombone and I never knew what he was snatching, so, but -- and the Cubans, they --they were trying to be noble. was fighting over one of them So I said, why don't you just try to get one of your own and not try to take his? And he said, "You aint no Cuban. Why don't you leave them alone!" So, we stayed up there until summer, we come around August. Around July.
